summary: The claim that the Earth revolves around the Sun is a fundamental and widely accepted scientific fact, forming the basis of the heliocentric model of our solar system. This understanding is supported by centuries of astronomical observation and research.

claim_analysis.claim: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
claim_analysis.explanation: Current scientific understanding, based on extensive evidence, confirms that the Earth orbits the Sun. This is a core tenet of the heliocentric model, which superseded earlier geocentric views. The Earth completes one full orbit around the Sun approximately every 365.25 days, which defines a year. The Earth's orbit is elliptical, not perfectly circular.

evidence: The Earth orbits around the sun every 365.25 days.
Earth revolves in orbit around the Sun in 365 days, 6 hours, 9 minutes with reference to the stars.
The Earth orbits (or revolves) around the sun. It takes 365.25 days to complete one orbit around the sun.
Earth's orbit around the Sun is not circular, but an ellipse that is slightly elongated.
Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of 149.60 million km (92.96 million mi)... One complete orbit takes 365.256 days (1 sidereal year).
The Earth completes one orbit every 365.242199 mean solar days.
While the heliocentric model correctly describes our solar system, it is now seen as part of a much larger cosmic framework.
As the Earth rotates, it also moves, or revolves, around the Sun. The Earth's path around the Sun is called its orbit. It takes the Earth one year, or 365 1/4 days, to completely orbit the Sun.
Heliocentrism is a superseded astronomical model that placed the Sun at the center of the universe, with the Earth and the planets in its orbit.
As Earth orbits the Sun, it completes one rotation every 23.9 hours. It takes 365.25 days to complete one trip around the Sun.
The Earth's orbit is an ellipse, and there is a slow change in its orientation.
Heliocentrism is an astronomical model that posits the Sun at the center of our solar system, with Earth and other planets orbiting around it.
The heliocentric theory is the idea that the Sun is at the centre of the solar system and that everything else – planets, asteroids, comets and the rest – revolves around it.
Heliocentrism, a cosmological model in which the Sun is assumed to lie at or near a central point (e.g., of the solar system or of the universe) while the Earth and other bodies revolve around it.
